title: Dense affine-open adic direct-image finiteness
statement: Fix a prime l. For a scheme V let Qbar_l,V be the sheaf of locally finite continuous functions to an algebraic closure of Q_l: locally on V the values lie in a finite extension of Q_l. Let AdicSheaf_l(V) be the abelian category of modules over this sheaf, and call such a sheaf constructible if Zariski locally it admits a finite partition by locally closed constructible subschemes on which it is pro-etale locally finite free. These are the concrete sheaf models of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Write D^b_c(V) for the objects of the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] which are bounded for its standard t-structure and have constructible cohomology. Let l be a prime and K an algebraically closed field with char K != l. Let t:W -> Spec K be quasi-compact and locally of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let j:Z -> W be a quasi-compact open immersion with dense topological range and with Z affine. For a constructible F in AdicSheaf_l(Z), Rj_*(F[0]) belongs to D^b_c(W).

proof.text: Use the exact faithful native-to-condensed encoding on the Noetherian source and target. Its cohomology and constructibility comparisons place F[0] in the bounded constructible category for the continuous algebraic-closure coefficient ring. Quasi-compact local finite type over K makes W Noetherian, and the quasi-compact open immersion makes Z Noetherian. No separatedness of W or positive-characteristic assumption is added.

For a finite field A killed by l, transport a bounded constructible pro-etale complex to the etale site using the fixed coefficient origin. Since l is a unit in K, apply finite-coefficient open direct-image finiteness. Transport back using the derived direct-image comparison. Bounded complexes over a field have finite Tor amplitude: all sheaves are flat and bounded truncation devissage applies. Use the normalized finite-discrete encoding and its tensor comparison to obtain the same assertions for internal condensed coefficients.

For a finite coefficient extension E/Q_l, its first residue quotient is a finite field killed by l. The integral residue criterion supplies derived completeness and bounded constructibility of the residue reduction of the integral input. Direct image preserves derived completeness and its canonical residue comparison is invertible. Apply the preceding finite-field result, then the integral residue criterion on W. This gives bounded constructibility of the integral image without imposing a fibre-dimension bound on an open immersion.

Transport integral constructibility between continuous coefficient models using their coefficient-ring isomorphisms and the integral local-finite-presentation/constant-model comparison. A bounded constructible complex over a finite rational coefficient field admits a constructible integral model. The qcqs integral-localization direct-image comparison and exact scalar extension carry bounded constructibility to its rational direct image. These coefficient transport helpers are reused from the proper finiteness module but require no properness.

Finite-coefficient descent represents a bounded constructible algebraic-closure-coefficient complex over a finite extension. The bounded-below qcqs Qbar coefficient-change mate identifies its direct image with the scalar extension of the finite-field image. Exact scalar extension preserves boundedness and constructibility. Finally the derived native encoding comparison and faithfulness reflect boundedness and constructible cohomology, giving the original statement.

      _root_.DerivedCategory.homologyProperty (adicConstructibleSheaf l W))
